foobar2000. It's lightweight and has a lot of plugins.
Winamp. Its no longer in development, but you can still find and use it.
The new owner of Winamp is developing it again. No time table of new releases though.
Winamp is proof that an old software still has what it takes.

Clementine, a linux port. It's rather bulky but I love its automatic scoring feature. Where it assigns a score to each song based on how many times you've listened or skipped it. The first time you listen to a track it receives a score of 50, then 75, 87 and so on in diminishing increments to 100. Combine that with a smart playlist that plays songs above a certain score means I get a constant stream of songs I like. If I grow tired of a song I skip it which lowers its score and eventually drops it below the playlist's threshold. Usually I jump between 'songs added in the past month' playlist and score above x playlists.
MPC-BE. Simple and out of the way, using Rainmeter and mouse button controls.
VLC Media Player, it's not fancy, but it's functional and plays every format in existence.

It's open source, does video as well as music, provides SUPER versatile tools, and works with just about every possible format.
